newsitem.title: RUSSIA: DeBakey sees Yeltsin on tennis court in 4 months.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey sees Yeltsin on tennis court in 4 months.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin could be back on the tennis court within four months, veteran U.S. cardiologist Michael DeBakey said on Wednesday.
But he warned the Russian president not to take things too fast after his seven-hour quintuple heart bypass.

"Everything is going quite well and of course it is very gratifying to see this happen because this is a very good sign that his prognosis is excellent," DeBakey, who was a consultant during Tuesday's operation, told CNN television.
"Within a matter of six weeks to two months, he could be back to doing pretty much what he wants," Debakey said.
Asked whether Yeltsin, 65, would be able to play his beloved tennis again, the U.S. surgeon answered: "I think in three or four months".
But DeBakey warned Yeltsin, who he said was alert and smiling when he saw him on Wednesday morning, to be careful.

"I told him (this morning) you must be very patient. I said -- You must be very patient, because I know that you want to get going. But I said - You know its very important that you follow the doctors' instructions," DeBakey told CNN.
"I said - You said (before the operation) you promised you would be a good patient. He smiled and said - I'm going to decide to be a good patient."

DeBakey, who performed the world's first bypass operation, said there were several possible complications for a heart patient after surgery, including bleeding, but added: "Fortunately none of them are taking place right now".
Without the surgery, DeBakey said, Yeltsin would definitely have been incapacitated. The surgery gave him a solid chance.
"I would say his chances of surviving another 10 to 15 years and leading a reasonably normal life is in the level of 60 percent."
The 88-year-old U.S. surgeon praised his pupil, Russian cardiologist Renat Akchurin, who led the operating team.
The Kremlin press service said doctors had taken Yeltsin off a lung ventilator on Wednesday morning, an important stage in the post-operation period.
A doctors council was due to meet on Wednesday morning to review Yeltsin's progress but there was no immediate information on their conclusions.
